chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: May Allah rectify you, is it that the one who loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and the one who hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him? He said: Yes. Then I said: By Allah, we surely hate death. He said: That is not where you think it goes; rather, it is at the time of direct encounter. When he sees what he loves, there is nothing more beloved to him than to advance, and Allah loves to meet him, and he loves to meet Allah at that time. And when he sees what he dislikes, there is nothing more hateful to him than to meet Allah, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, hates to meet him.
ai.seo_question: Why do Muslims hate death if they love to meet Allah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this nuance in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, distinguishing between the general aversion to the cessation of worldly life (death) and the specific spiritual state of readiness for divine presence (liqa’). The Imam clarifies that the love or hatred of the meeting is contingent upon the believer's spiritual condition at the moment of direct encounter, where the sight of divine reward or punishment determines their ultimate affection for Allah. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accounting) to ensure one's heart is prepared for the actuality of the meeting, not just the concept of death.
